name: Comfy Image - WordPress ComfyUI Integration
summary: A WordPress plugin that enables Gutenberg users to generate and insert images using a remote ComfyUI instance via slash commands or a block widget.
goals: Let editors generate images on-the-fly inside Gutenberg using ComfyUI
Expose a slash command `/comfy` and a Gutenberg block to create images from text prompts
Provide an admin UI to configure ComfyUI endpoint, workflow templates and media options
Save generated images to the WP Media Library by default and insert them into posts/pages
primary_features: Slash-command prompt: `/comfy <description>` inside Gutenberg to call ComfyUI (planned)
Gutenberg block: dedicated UI for prompt + basic settings (seed, steps) — implemented (minimal)
Admin settings page to set ComfyUI URL, default workflow, and save-to-media behavior — implemented
Server-side REST endpoints that submit workflows, poll for completion, fetch results, and import into WP Media — implemented
Client-side UX: progress updates and image insertion into post content — implemented (basic)
secondary_features: Multiple workflow templates (shop, hero images, avatars, etc.)
CORS and host allowlist for ComfyUI integration
Admin usage logs and generated-image audit

tech_stack.comfyui: ComfyUI HTTP API (upload, prompt, history, view)

comfyui_integration.notes: Workflows are JSON objects; the plugin ships an example template under templates/. The plugin proxies submit/history/view calls and supports server-side import of resulting images into WP Media.

security_considerations: Use `check_ajax_referer` for AJAX endpoints where appropriate and protect REST routes if needed
Sanitize all inputs (`sanitize_text_field`, `esc_url_raw`) and validate remote responses
Restrict ComfyUI host via admin settings and optionally an allowlist
When saving images to media, verify MIME and use WordPress upload APIs

development_state.scaffold: created (basic plugin files, settings page, templates)
development_state.endpoints: REST endpoints implemented: submit-workflow, check-status, fetch-image (import to media)
development_state.gutenberg_block: Minimal block implemented (assets/block.js) that submits workflows, polls for results and inserts images
development_state.upload_endpoint: stub (multipart upload forwarding to ComfyUI pending)
development_state.notes: This is an initial working prototype: settings UI, REST proxy endpoints, image import, and a basic Gutenberg block are implemented. Security hardening, rate-limiting, UX polish, and tests remain to be added.

todo.title: Build Gutenberg block and slash command
Implement image UI and media handling
Write tests, docs and package plugin

requirements: WordPress development environment (LocalWP, Docker, or WP-CLI)
ComfyUI instance accessible from the host running WordPress
steps: Copy the plugin folder into wp-content/plugins/comfy-image
Activate the plugin in WP Admin > Plugins
Open Settings > Comfy Image and confirm or update the ComfyUI Base URL
Open Gutenberg editor, add the 'Comfy Image' block, enter a prompt and click Generate
